## Problem

You are about to download an image and the release names twelve
targets — profiles × formats × architectures — and you want to pick
once, correctly, by role: not too little tooling to work with, not
gigabytes of lab weight you will never fire, and no desktop on a box
that only an agent will ever touch. Choosing a profile IS choosing
your image; make it a decision, not a guess.

## Solution

Match your role to the profile; the image-matrix table then names the
exact artefact and its size budget:

| Profile | Carries | Choose it when |
|---|---|---|
| `minimal` | the CORE substrate — kernel, base userland, hardening, safety defaults, desktop, CLI & menu engines; no tool categories enabled (categories are added declaratively later) | you are learning the system, building a hardened base, or you know exactly which categories you will enable |
| `redteam-ai` | the AI red-team lab scope — ATTACK core plus its OPS/DEFENCE pairings | you are following the cookbook's scanning and pair recipes, or doing LLM red-team engagements |
| `full` | the complete live catalogue ("kali-everything" lab scope) | you are running the live demonstrator, or want every category present to explore |
| `headless-agent` | base + CLI only, no desktop; the qcow2 grows at first boot | you are standing up an automation host or an agent-operated box (O-7 grants apply) |

The budget table (from the declared build matrix — every artefact's
budget is enforced by construction):

| Target (`nix build .#<ref>`) | Profile | System | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kailash-images-qemu-minimal` / `-iso-minimal` | minimal | x86_64 | ≤4 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-redteam-ai` / `-iso-redteam-ai` | redteam-ai | x86_64 | ≤8 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-full` / `-iso-full` | full | x86_64 | ≤10 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-headless-agent` / `-iso-headless-agent` | headless-agent | x86_64 | ≤1.5 GB |
| `kailash-images-…-aarch64-minimal` (qemu + iso) | minimal | aarch64 | ≤4 GB |
| `kailash-images-…-aarch64-headless-agent` (qemu + iso) | headless-agent | aarch64 | ≤1.5 GB |

Which profile for which cookbook section:

| Cookbook section | Fits profile | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Scanning | `redteam-ai` | the a-02 scanner stack (garak…) rides the profile |
| Attack–defence pairs | `redteam-ai` | the pair thesis needs the OPS target + ATTACK probe (pair recipes touching non-shipped postures read the module per release) |
| Ops | `redteam-ai` or `full` | serving (o-04/o-02) ships with the lab scope |
| Administrator | any — `minimal` is the honest start | admin recipes act on the base system, not a category |

On the booted system, confirm the choice the release declares:

```bash
kailash profile list
```

Expected output shape (one row per profile, TAB-separated):

```
<name>	<layers-summary>	<description>
```

## Discussion

- **The profile is baked into the image name:** a release asset reads
  `kailash-<tag>-kailash-<profile>.<ext>` — you cannot pick a profile
  at boot; you pick it at download (or pull the matching flake ref).
  That is why this recipe is a download-time decision, not a
  post-boot one.
- **Categories beat profiles for precision:** between `redteam-ai`
  and `full`, prefer the former unless you specifically want the
  complete catalogue; anything narrower still comes as a declarative
  category enablement + rebuild (see
  [Enable your first category](first-category.html)) — the same
  category modules the profiles are composed from.
- **Data packs are never part of the choice:** wordlists, SDR and
  other corpora ride opt-in `kailash-data.*` derivations and are
  excluded from every default image by construction — no profile
  carries them, and no profile choice can pull them in behind your
  back (see
  [Refresh wordlists and data packs](../admin/data-packs.html)).
- **Safety posture is identical across profiles:** the double-key
  lab-mode gate and the `requires-target` refusals are properties of
  the manifest rows and the base safety module, not of the profile you
  chose — `full` is not "more dangerous", only "more present".
- **The aarch64 picture:** the arm slice is the arch strategy (x86
  hosted builds, arm built locally on Apple Silicon);
  `redteam-ai`/`full` aarch64 rows land with the KA-36 slice-2 sweep —
  check the release's own artefact table before planning an arm lab.
- **`headless-agent` grows:** the qcow2 budget is the boot-time floor;
  the store grows as the agent enables categories and rebuilds. Budget
  the host disk, not just the download.
